transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-28
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marcus (HavenWell CTO), Sofia (Head of ML), David (Platform)
---
Summary: quick product walkthrough focused on the model catalog (open models), benchmarks, and compatibility matrices. Covered API, Console, and Redwood Optimize recommendations for quantization and batching. Customer interested in expected latency/cost tradeoffs and private/VPC deployment feasibility for PHI workloads.
Topics: model variants, benchmarks (latency/cost), dedicated vs hosted, VPC/private, security (SOC2/KMS), POC scope, next steps.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone good afternoon, thanks for joining, you can hear me ok?
[00:06] Marcus: yeah loud and clear thanks for doing this.
[00:10] Jordan: cool, so quick agenda, we'll do a 20 minute demo of the model catalog + console, Priya will jump into compatibility / benchmarks, then Q&A and next steps. Sound good?
[00:20] Sofia: yep that works for us.

[01:05] Priya: alright i'm going to share my screen now. Uh quick note, i'm going to call out a couple of open-source models in the catalog — we've got smaller quantized variants, float16 and int8 where applicable, and then larger context models for long form.
[01:30] Speaker 1: (inaudible) you said int 8, do you mean Q4_0 or Q8?
[01:35] Priya: yeah so we have a couple of quantization profiles — Q4_0, Q4_KMV, and Q8 on some architectures. the console exposes recommended profiles per model and per workload.

[02:10] Jordan: the model catalog page here — quick tour: you can filter by task (chat, completion, embeddings), by latency tier, and by license (apache, mit, etc). we also surface redwood-verified perf profiles — these are our internal benchmarks for throughput/latency on different GPUs.
[02:45] Marcus: are those benchmarks public? do you share raw numbers?
[02:50] Priya: we can share the csv — i'll attach the raw benchmark spreadsheet after the call. tbh the console shows summarised numbers but the raw is available for POC partners.

[04:00] David: curious about compatibility — our infra currently uses Triton and KFServing, any gotchas in switching to Redwood Dedicated or Private?
[04:12] Priya: good question. compatibility matrix is in the docs — in short, we support standard model formats (pt, ggml, onnx) and for dedicated/private we deploy on our runtime which is optimized (we do kernel selection and compilation) but you can bring model artifacts with expected formats. if you're using Triton specifics you'll want to check iteration on custom ops but most OSS causal models are straightforward.
[04:50] Sofia: how do you handle KV cache and prefix caching with long-running chat sessions? latency sensitive for us.
[04:57] Priya: we have two mechanisms: automatic KV cache reuse inside a session and prefix caching for common prompts. that reduces tokens served and is configurable per-route in the console.

[06:00] Jordan: okay moving into benchmarks — Priya is going to show 1k token generation tests across a few open models.
[06:10] Priya: so here's a quick table — model A (smaller, 7b family), model B (13b), model C (70b fractional), run on an A100-ish and on a 4090 cluster; latency numbers are median p50 and p95. keep in mind these are our internal runs with batching disabled to show single-request latencies.
[06:45] Priya: e.g., 7b int8 -> p50 ~ 120ms, p95 ~ 240ms on dedicated GPU; 13b q4_kmv p50 ~ 180ms p95 ~ 420ms; 70b float16 p50 ~ 900ms p95 ~ 1.8s. costs scale accordingly.
[07:10] Marcus: those p95s on 70b are a bit high for us, we usually target sub-800ms for critical paths. what's the tradeoff to get there?
[07:18] Priya: you can either use smaller model variant, or use Redwood Optimize suggestions: quantize to Q4_KMV or Q8 where possible, and use sharded KV cache and autoscale to reserved capacity (Dedicated) to reduce queuing. also you can do a serving-time fallback to a cheaper model for non-critical calls.

[08:00] Speaker 2: (laughs) we have the same debate internal.
[08:05] David: can you clarify the fallback? is it automatic?
[08:09] Jordan: it's policy-driven, you can set routing by latency or cost. so a request that exceeds Xms can fallback to a pinned cheaper variant, or go to a different region. it's all configurable in route policies in the console.

[09:00] Sofia: security stuff — if we need PHI, can Redwood Private run in our VPC, and do you support our KMS/HSM?
[09:08] Priya: yes Redwood Private supports customer-managed networking, private control plane, and we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM options). we also produce audit logs and can meet SOC 2 requirements — we have a compliance pack we share during procurement.
[09:38] Marcus: what about data retention and log scrubbing? we need low retention and optional field redaction.
[09:45] Jordan: that's supported — retention windows configurable per deployment and per-tenant. we also have token-level filtering in the ingest pipeline for PII redaction.

[11:00] Priya: back to compat matrix — i'll scroll. this shows model architecture vs supported runtime features: quantization supported, KV cache supported, multi-gpu sharding, and memory footprint per quant profile. models with custom CUDA kernels might have fewer quant options and we mark them as 'compat caveat'.
[11:40] Marcus: is that caveat usually a blocker?
[11:44] Priya: usually not for common LLMs, but if you rely on a very custom op we run a compatibility pass during onboarding and let you know if we need to ship a custom kernel.

[13:10] Jordan: quick demo of the API — standard REST call for generation, streaming supported, function calling available, and you can pin model_version in the request. you can also pass an expected latency hint and an allowed cost budget header — that'll feed into routing decisions.
[13:40] David: that 'cost budget' header, is that internal accounting or does it change model selection?
[13:45] Priya: it changes routing — it tells the platform to try cheaper model variants or use cached outputs if available. it's part of Redwood Optimize features.

[15:00] Sofia: do you surface token-level cost on the console? we'd like to track unit economics.
[15:06] Jordan: yes per-route model + token breakdown in the console; it's pretty granular. you can also export to CSV for FinOps analysis.

[16:20] Priya: show a sample Optimize recommendation — the Optimize tab suggests batching size, quant profile, and expected token cost savings. it will say e.g., 'recommend Q4_KMV + batch 4 -> estimated 38% token cost reduction for chat workload with p50 ~ unchanged'.
[16:50] Marcus: how confident are those estimates? we don't want to degrade quality.
[16:54] Priya: recommendations are based on historical evals, but we surface expected quality delta and give you a canary/rollout flow to test a small % of traffic. quality regression alerts are tied to prompt sets.

[18:00] David: what's the typical POC? we want to run a two week pilot with a slice of traffic and measure latency and quality.
[18:07] Jordan: that's exactly what we do — 2 week POC with benchmark harness, we run your sample traffic and compare to baseline, produce a report. Priya will run the compatibility checks during onboarding.

[19:20] Sofia: any limits on model licensing for commercial usage? some of our legal team cares.
[19:27] Jordan: the catalog surfaces license type; for commercial that requires different licensing we flag it. we'll loop in legal if something is ambiguous.

[20:30] Priya: quick demo of the compatibility matrix link — (link: https://redwood.ai/internal/compatibility/havenwell) — note: placeholder link will be replaced with the shared doc.
[20:50] Speaker 1: link doesn't work for me.
[20:55] Jordan: that was a sample internal link, we'll share public copy.

[22:00] Marcus: can you speak to SLA/uptime for Dedicated? we need 99.9 for a single region.
[22:06] Jordan: Dedicated comes with SLA options; 99.9 is typical on reserved capacity. Private on-prem can be negotiated with SRE support.

[23:10] David: cost model — do you charge per-token for hosted and a flat for dedicated?
[23:15] Jordan: hosted is usage-based per-token + per-embedding units, Dedicated is reserved capacity pricing (monthly commit) plus smaller usage overages. we'll send a comparison spreadsheet.

[24:45] Priya: here's an example of a benchmark CSV row — model, quant_profile, hw_type, p50_ms, p95_ms, tokens_per_sec. i'll share full spreadsheet.
[25:20] Sofia: for our latency-sensitive endpoints we usually also budget for cold-starts, how are those handled?
[25:25] Priya: warm pools in Dedicated, and fast cold-starts on hosted using cached kernels. we can keep warm containers pinned for critical routes.

[26:40] Jordan: quick question — what are your top success criteria for this POC?
[26:46] Marcus: sub-800ms p95 for critical path, cost < $0.02 per 1k tokens (example), and no PHI leakage, full audit logs.
[26:55] Sofia: and model quality comparable to our current baseline (we'll share eval prompts).

[28:10] Priya: noted, we'll run targeted benchmarks and a regression eval against your prompts.

[29:00] David: anything we should be aware of in terms of infra changes? we like to avoid major changes to CI/CD.
[29:06] Priya: for Private you'll likely need network peering and KMS setup, plus access for our onboarding team. for Dedicated it's mostly a config and route setup; we provide terraform modules and CI examples.

[31:00] Jordan: ok we're approaching time — wanted to call out a couple of typical objections: latency vs cost, and whether to go private vs hosted. often the path is start hosted or dedicated POC, then migrate to Private if compliance requires.
[31:20] Marcus: that makes sense.

[32:15] Sofia: last question: how do you measure quality regressions in Optimize? is it string match or embedding distance?
[32:22] Priya: we use a combination: rubric-based evals, embedding-based similarity, and application-level metrics (click-through, acceptance). you can plug in your own eval harness.

[33:40] Jordan: quick recap — Priya will share benchmarks + compatibility matrix and link; I'll send pricing and hosted vs dedicated comparison. HavenWell to provide traffic profile and PII requirements. We'll aim to start a 2-week POC in mid-Oct.

[34:10] Speaker 2: (crosstalk) thats great, thanks.
[34:30] Marcus: thanks everyone, this was helpful. we'll try to get the eval prompts to you by next week.

[35:15] Jordan: perfect, and we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the POC kickoff.

[36:00] Priya: one more thing — on the rollout side, we support canary, A/B and automatic fallback based on model-level error rates and latency. you'll get tracing hooks to your observability stack.
[36:20] David: which tracing providers? we use Datadog and Lightstep.
[36:24] Priya: both supported via open telemetry exporters.

[38:00] Sofia: any red flags on our side in terms of feasibility?
[38:05] Priya: nothing major from what you've said. the main items are the sample traffic and clarifying PHI retention. We'll validate a few models in the compatibility pass.

[40:00] Jordan: ok final recap and next steps, i'll capture in email. Thanks everyone.
[40:10] Marcus: thanks, bye.
[40:14] Sofia: bye.
[40:17] David: thanks.
---
End of transcript.
